Prevention: When selecting planting sites, avoid fields infested with termites
For small, localized areas with infestation, sterilize soil before planting (e.g., with hot water)
Plant basil ( Ocimum spp. ) as a barrier to repel termites.
Leave space between basil and crop because this native plant may reduce growth/ survival of cassava if grown too close
Early burning of vegetation before planting
Phytosanitary measures (for example, do not move infested material)
If mulch material is used, do not mulch close to the cassava plant as this will attract termites
Keep soil moist in the dry season
Monitoring: Regular visitation to farms during the dry season
Identify termite mounds and pay close attention to the cassava plants nearest to those mounds
Look for damage signs: for example, mud on stems or cuts on stems
Uproot young plants that fail to sprout to check for termites
Direct Control: Collect driver ants and put them in areas affected by termites
Physically destroy colonies by digging out white ant hills/ termite mounds.
Apply wood ash to the base of the plant.
Restrictions: Spray around the edges of the field to prevent termites from entering the crop or spot treat infestations within the crop.; Moderately hazardous (WHO Class
